title: Reconcile diverged Pilobol.us build.py: effects work vs deploy branch

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Two copies of /web/build.py have diverged and BOTH have something the other needs. Neither is a superset. Do not blindly take either side.

COPY A - Pilobol.us main branch, commit c9a8823 (rescued from untracked; was committed nowhere before today):
  + the generative effects work: physarum-v17/v5, reaction-diffusion, cellular-automata, background-manager, cinematic-gallery, organic-image, the effects/ pages, sample imagery, pilobil-theme-v10.css (~5,200 lines)
  + an 'Effects Index' nav item
  - still says 'Pilobil.us' - the SUPERSEDED spelling. Decided name is Pilobol.us (see PPY-17fcfc: 'The public domain is pilobol.us ... do not relitigate').
  - NO theme-toggle script
  - NEVER copies assets/ or css/ into dist/ - so a clean build from this copy yields HTML with no styles and no JS
  - globally un-escapes < > " in Markus output - see PPY-2d0e52, must not survive reconciliation

COPY B - Pilobol.us-worktrees/PPY-17fcfc-static-hosting, branch cursor/feature/PPY-17fcfc-amplify-static-3af6 (what production deploys):
  + correct 'Pilobol.us' spelling throughout
  + theme-toggle script (verified working in a browser: data-theme flips, localStorage 'pilobil-theme' persists across navigation)
  + DOES copy assets/ and css/ into dist/ (lines ~124-130)
  + has amplify.yml
  - NONE of the effects work

CONSEQUENCE OF THE MISSING COPY STEP: I ran copy A's build.py. It emitted 20 files, but dist/assets/ still contained a STALE physarum-v8.js while background-manager.js requests physarum-v17.js, which was never copied. The effect is broken in that build output. dist only looked right because earlier one-shot scripts had hand-copied files into it. Copy A's dist is not reproducible from copy A's build.py.

TARGET: one build.py with copy B's correctness (name, theme toggle, asset/css copy, amplify.yml) PLUS copy A's effects, and WITHOUT the unescape hack - replace it per PPY-2d0e52 option (b): put effect scaffolding in the trusted page shell and let Markdown only name the effect to mount.

ACCEPTANCE: rm -rf web/dist && python3 web/build.py produces a complete, correct site - styles present, physarum-v17 present and loading, theme toggle working, 'Pilobol.us' spelling throughout - with no manual file copying.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
MORE DAMAGE FOUND in the main-tree build.py while fixing the click bug. This copy is worse than first reported; do not treat it as a candidate to keep.

1. main() NEVER BUILDS index.html OR THE ARTICLES. It only writes effects/*.html. Proven: after running it, web/dist/effects/index.html was rewritten at 13:36 while web/dist/index.html still showed 12:53. The front page and both articles in dist are ORPHANED artifacts that this script cannot regenerate - they survive only because earlier one-shot scripts hand-wrote them.

2. Lines ~103-118 and ~122-137 are a VERBATIM DUPLICATE of each other: the effects index and the effects loop are both built twice per run.

3. Combined with the already-reported missing assets/css copy step, 'rm -rf web/dist && python3 web/build.py' does not produce a working site from this copy. Not close.

The deploy branch copy (cursor/feature/PPY-17fcfc-amplify-static-3af6) does build index and articles, copies assets and css, and has the theme toggle and the correct Pilobol.us spelling. RECONCILIATION DIRECTION IS SETTLED: take the deploy branch's build.py as the base and port the effects work onto it. Do not try to repair the main-tree copy.

WHAT I ADDED to the main-tree copy (port these forward, they are small and worth keeping):
- css_version() and ?v=<mtime> cache-busting on both stylesheet links. Without it a CSS fix silently appears not to work - that cost real time today, and there is a serve_nocache.py in tools/oneshot/ showing this has bitten before.

STILL TO PORT and NOT yet done: removing the global HTML unescape (PPY-2d0e52).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
PROGRESS: Pilobol.us now builds through PAPYRUS'S renderer. This closes the gap where production demonstrated Markus but not Papyrus's Markus renderer.

PAPYRUS SIDE (commit e428941) - made the renderer usable by a publication other than Papyrus itself:
- SiteChrome in shell.py: per-publication site_name, tagline, footer_html, and chrome scripts. Scripts are emitted before </body>, depth-prefixed like nav links, and are NEVER derived from article Markdown - that boundary is deliberate and is the correct answer to PPY-2d0e52's unescape hack.
- site_css is a parameter now instead of a hardcoded constant.
- sections=(...) discovers optional <content>/<section>/*.md alongside articles/; absent sections are skipped rather than raising.
- Stylesheet links carry ?v=<newest css mtime>.
Defaults reproduce Papyrus's own site exactly. Tests pass, lint and typecheck clean.

PILOBOL SIDE (commit 95347f2): web/build_via_papyrus.py. The pod contributes ONLY its identity; rendering, nav, asset copying, CSS vendoring and cache-busting all come from the shared renderer. Builds all 7 pages (index, 2 articles, 4 effects). Verified serving on :8903 - assets 200, both stylesheets 200, physarum-v17.js 200, effect scripts wired, every link hit-tests to its own <a>. Also corrected the superseded 'Pilobil.us' spelling in content.

NOT YET SWITCHED IN PRODUCTION, deliberately. One real blocker remains:

THEME CSS CLASS MISMATCH. pilobil-theme-v10.css styles .pilo-masthead / .pilo-wordmark / .pilo-nav (3, 3 and 4 occurrences). Papyrus's shell emits .markus-site-masthead / .markus-site-wordmark / .markus-site-nav (0 occurrences in the theme). Zero overlap, so under Papyrus's renderer the masthead and nav render unstyled. The theme was written against the bespoke build's markup.

THAT IS A DESIGN-TRACK DECISION but the MECHANISM is architectural, so decide it here:
(a) Update the Pilobol theme to target Papyrus's shell classes. Simplest; makes the shell's class names the contract for every publication.
(b) Let SiteChrome supply masthead/footer markup so a publication owns its own chrome classes. More flexible, more surface, and risks each publication reinventing the shell.
Recommend (a) - one documented set of shell class names that themes target, consistent with how site_css already layers over vendored Markus CSS.

Once that lands, switching amplify.yml from 'cd web && python3 build.py' to the Papyrus renderer is a one-line change, and the legacy build.py (which cannot rebuild its own front page) can be deleted.
